title: Line Plots and Fraction Operations
short: Use a line plot to find totals and fair shares.

blocks.html: In Grade 4 you made line plots of measurements in eighths. Now that you can add fractions with unlike denominators, a line plot can answer questions like “how much in all?” and “how much would each get if it were shared evenly?”
Each X is one measurement. To find a total, multiply each value by the number of X marks above it and add. To share the total equally, divide it by the number of measurements.

Three X marks above $\frac{3}{8}$ stand for $\frac{3}{8} + \frac{3}{8} + \frac{3}{8}$, which is $3 \times \frac{3}{8} = \frac{9}{8}$. Adding column by column is just grouping equal values. Sharing equally means pouring everything together and splitting it: total $\div$ number of beakers.

blocks.title: The total
blocks.q: Use the line plot above. How much water is there in all?

blocks.title: Share equally
blocks.q: If all of that water were poured back into the 8 beakers equally, how much would each hold?
steps: Divide the total by the number of beakers: $3 \div 8$.

blocks.title: Greatest minus least
blocks.q: How much more is in the fullest beaker than the emptiest?

blocks.html: Adding only the values on the scale and ignoring how many X marks are stacked above each. Three marks at $\frac{3}{8}$ count three times. Check: count the X marks first; the total has to use every one.
